claim: The `juju-info` endpoint is the standard mechanism used by general-purpose machine subordinates that need to ride along on every machine of a principal but do not have any application-specific data to exchange.
URI vs. label:) I as a user might create a secret with a name that makes sense to me, for example, `my-api-key`.
When you deploy an application on a machine, there is usually one unit per machine.
The convention is for a subordinate to name its own `requires` endpoint `juju-info`, but any name can be used (for example: `info`, `general-info`); it just needs to use interface `juju-info`.
A cross-model relation has two sides: the offering side (aka "offerer") and the consume side (aka 'saas').
It is available as an opt-in to both machine  and Kubernetes models.
A minimum configuration must include the `endpoint`, `namespace`, and `ca-cert`.
prior_note: mandatory are endpoint and namespace; ca-cert optional

claim: Note that, in peer relations, all permissions related to the remote application are turned inwards and become permissions related to the local application.

The URI is returned to the caller so they can then use it in subsequent actions (for example, a charm might grant permission to that secret using the URI and then put the URI in relation data).
It does not make a difference which side of the relation (provider or requirer) is the offerer and which is the saas - the two are interchangeable.
